seoDescription: Learn how to add user registration to a Django project by creating a dedicated accounts app, wiring URLconf entries, building a register view, and rendering a simple HTML registration form tied to Django's built-in auth user model. This tutorial covers app creation, URL inclusion, view rendering, CSRF token use, and the required form fields (username, password, email, name) so you can prepare user signups and extend to login/logout.

chapters.title: Intro and why authentication matters
chapters.description: Sets up the motivation for adding login and registration to the Django travel app and the plan for separate user accounts.

chapters.title: User roles and choosing where to place auth
chapters.description: Discusses admin vs normal users, options for creating accounts manually or via registration forms, and why a separate accounts module can be useful.

chapters.title: Preparing the environment and creating the accounts app
chapters.description: Shows working in the virtual environment, starting the Django server, and creating a new app named accounts to hold authentication views and URLs.

chapters.title: Adding accounts URLs and initial view
chapters.description: Creates accounts/urls.py by copying patterns, adds URL include in project URLs so accounts routes are served under /accounts/, and scaffolds a register view.

chapters.title: Rendering the register template and building the form
chapters.description: Implements the register view to render register.html, creates a simple HTML registration template with CSRF token and adds fields for first name, last name, username, email, password and confirm password plus submit button.

summary:
## Key Concepts

- **Accounts app**: Create a dedicated Django app (accounts) for authentication to keep auth logic modular and reusable across projects.

- **Project URL inclusion**: Add path('accounts/', include('accounts.urls')) to the project's urls.py so accounts routes are served under /accounts/ (e.g., /accounts/register).

- **Views**: Scaffold a register view that accepts a request and returns render(request, 'register.html') — views must return HttpResponse or render results.

- **Templates and form**: Build a simple register.html with an HTML form using method="post", include **{% csrf_token %}**, and provide input fields matching Django's auth_user columns: **first_name**, **last_name**, **username**, **email**, **password1**, **password2**. Add a submit input for registration.

- **Django auth model**: The built-in **auth_user** table already provides username, password, first_name, last_name, email, and date_joined. You can use this instead of creating a custom user model for basic registration.

> [!TIP]
> Naming form input fields to match auth_user field names (username, first_name, last_name, email) simplifies mapping when you later create user objects.

> [!NOTE]
> The tutorial stops before saving submitted form data; implementing backend validation, password hashing, and user creation will be covered in follow-up material.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Ensure the CSRF token is present in POST forms; otherwise Django will reject submissions. Also remember to return an HttpResponse from every view.
